title: Reservoir-forecast quilted microbatch throttler and KV tiered eviction strategy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and prototype a reservoir-forecast based microbatch admission controller that "quilts" microbatches across token-slots to reduce oscillation at high QPS, paired with a KV-tiered eviction and staged GPU memory compaction plan. Goal: preserve P95/P99 latency SLOs while increasing sustained throughput under bursty/high QPS workloads and minimizing KV thrash/eviction storms.
acceptance_criteria: New controller deployed behind feature flag and enabled in canary cluster
Under synthetic high-QPS traffic (10-30% above baseline), P95 gen latency degradation <= 10% and P99 <= 25% compared to baseline
KV eviction rate (evictions/sec) reduced by >= 30% in steady-state bursts compared to current strategy
No unrecoverable OOMs in canary for 72h of bounded stress tests
Observability: new dashboards for reservoir headroom, quilted-batch size distribution, tenant defer ratio, and staged compaction latency
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Simulation (2 days) - offline simulator that replays production QPS traces and compares current admission vs reservoir-forecast controller
Phase 1: Core controller (5 days) - implement reservoir EWMA + forecast horizon, quilting allocator that spreads microbatch token assignments into soft time-slices to avoid synchronous flushes
Phase 2: KV tiering policy (3 days) - implement tenant-weighted score combining recency, frequency, and predicted reuse from forecast; expose aggressive/lenient tiers
Phase 3: GPU staged compaction (3 days) - introduce light compaction path before heavy eviction and a non-blocking reclamation path to reclaim small slabs
Phase 4: Canaries & metrics (3 days) - feature flag rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% within dedicated cluster; add dashboards and anomaly alerts
Phase 5: Postmortem & tuning (2 days) - collect telemetry and tune EWMA alpha, forecast horizon, quilting slice length
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservoir math and admission gating
Integration tests: end-to-end request flow with mocked GPU allocator and KV store
Load tests: replay of 7 representative production traces (evening, morning burst, holiday peak, multi-tenant hotshot)
Chaos tests: introduce random KV backend latency spikes and verify graceful degradation
Safety rollbacks: automatic fallback to baseline admission policy on error budget burn or OOM alerts
metrics: Microbatch size distribution (mean, median, 95th) and quilted slice variance
KV eviction rate (evictions/sec) and avg items/eviction
Reservoir headroom estimate and forecast error (MSE)
Tenant defer ratio and request rejection rate
GPU memory reclaim latency (light vs heavy compaction)
risks: Forecast error can cause mis-admission leading to transient latencies — mitigated by conservative headroom and short horizon
Quilting introduces micro-delay for tail-sensitive tenants — mitigated by tenant weight bypass where SLA required
Complexity of KV-tier scoring might increase CPU cost — we will offload scoring to a sampling path and cache scores
Staged compaction could interact poorly with existing slab allocator; ensure non-blocking light path and gradual rollout
